issues.failure_explanation: Remark 2 claims that the Neumann eigenvalue gap satisfies the two-sided exponential bound |\mu_k^{R,N} - \lambda_k| \le C_k' e^{-\alpha_k' R}. The argument fails for three independent reasons: (1) for k >= 2, the Rayleigh quotient of a single restricted eigenfunction u_k|_{D(R)} does not furnish an upper bound for the k-th Neumann eigenvalue \mu_k^{R,N}; (2) Proposition 2 states \lambda_k >= \mu_k^{R,N}(1 - \Lambda_k/\sigma(R)), which rearranges to \mu_k^{R,N} <= \lambda_k / (1 - \Lambda_k/\sigma(R)), i.e., an upper bound on \mu_k^{R,N}, not a lower bound. Combining two upper bounds on \mu_k^{R,N} provides no lower bound on \mu_k^{R,N} and cannot yield a two-sided bound; and (3) the correction factor in Proposition 2 is algebraic in R (O(1/\sigma(R)) = O(R^{-4}) or O(R^{-2})), so even if it provided an opposite inequality, it could not establish an exponential rate.

    |\lambda_k^{R,\mathrm{Dir}}-\lambda_k|\le C_k e^{-\alpha_k R},\quad
    |\mu_k^{R,N}-\lambda_k|\le C_k' e^{-\alpha_k' R}.
    \label{eq:agmon-both}
  \end{equation}

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must supply a separate lower bound establishing exponential convergence of \mu_k^{R,N} to \lambda_k (e.g. via IMS localization formulas or Agmon interior estimates), or withdraw the claim in (12) that Proposition 2 and the single Rayleigh quotient imply two-sided exponential convergence for \mu_k^{R,N}.
issues.overall_effect: The two-sided exponential convergence estimate for the truncated Neumann eigenvalues in (12) is unproven and unsupported by the arguments in the text.
issues.title: Invalid deduction of two-sided exponential convergence for Neumann eigenvalues
issues.why_classification: The source provides no proof or machinery to establish a two-sided exponential bound (or any lower bound) on \mu_k^{R,N} - \lambda_k; establishing the primary claim of Remark 2 would require substantial new proof architecture beyond what is in the paper, or abandoning the claim.
